clue.text: Here butterfly may be seen with it

definitions.meaning: the butterfly is a swimming stroke, so it is seen out in the water among swimmers
with it means fashionable and up to date, abreast of the current trend

explanation.surface: A nature-lover points out where a butterfly might be spotted alongside something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butterfly' wants to be an insect; here it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being abreast of fashion is likened to keeping up with the current, and a stroke is literally performed in the water.

clue.text: Northerner has change of heart, don't you agree?

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for the northerner is swapped for a different one

parts.note: an Inuit is one of the Arctic peoples of the far north

explanation.surface: Someone from the north has a change of mind and asks for agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inuit's central U becomes N. INNIT is British slang tag-question for 'isn't it?', used to seek agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang tag-question used in colloquial British speech to seek assent, a contraction of isn't it.

clue.text: Put out hot water

definitions.meaning: to put someone out is to inconvenience or bother them
being in hot water means being in difficulty

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means inconvenience someone; as a noun it means a difficult predicament, which is what hot water idiomatically denotes.

clue.text: Enforced absence of team left in outlying parts of empire

indicators.note: the team and the left are placed inside the outer letters
outlying parts are the outermost letters of the following word

parts.note: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Banishment of a sports side that stayed behind in the empire's distant provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: Banishment from one's homeland is a forced absence imposed by authority.

clue.text: Get rid of insignificant question in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the phrase is spoken and its sound is what counts

parts.note: wee means tiny and a doubt is a question, so a small query

explanation.surface: Dismiss a trivial query when it comes up in a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Wee (Scottish for small) plus doubt, said aloud, sounds like the phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove unwanted items from a group, as a gardener pulls unwanted plants, is to eliminate them.

clue.text: Falsify accounts, getting endless prison term reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters are looked at again and rearranged
endless means the final letter of the following word is cut off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fraudster cooks the books after his jail sentence is reconsidered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the N of PRISON; 'reviewed' rearranges PRISO plus TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a false account of events or figures is to falsify a report.

clue.text: Transport for British general

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of General Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A request for a vehicle to carry a British army commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle is a means of getting around, an example of transport.

clue.text: Small Italian home surrounded by short grass

indicators.note: surrounded by means the home is enclosed by the shortened grass
short means the last letter of the grass is cut off

parts.note: bamboo is a giant grass
in means at home

explanation.surface: A small Italian house ringed by low-cut lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the final letter of the grass; 'Small' wants to modify Italian, but the whole phrase is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian word for a baby or little child, a small Italian person.

clue.text: Don't obstruct slippery eel packer

indicators.note: slippery suggests the letters slide about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's slimy eel-boxer is told to stay out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: The road-sign instruction tells drivers to leave a space unblocked.

clue.text: Heartlessly omniscient, getting sorted immediately

indicators.note: sorted means the remaining letters are put into a new order
heartlessly means the central two letters of the next word are removed

explanation.surface: An all-knowing being, without compassion, gets things fixed at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' removes the middle SC of OMNISCIENT; 'sorted' rearranges OMNIIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning very quickly, with practically no delay.

clue.text: Milne's false pretender given fruitcake

indicators.note: false indicates the letters are not in their true order

explanation.surface: A. A. Milne's fake claimant to the throne is handed a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretender' also describes the answer: Lambert Simnel claimed the English throne in 1487. A simnel cake is a British Easter fruitcake topped with marzipan.
explanation.definitionFit: Name of a rich marzipan-layered cake traditionally eaten in Britain at Easter or Mothering Sunday.

clue.text: Where groom may be found in uniform

definitions.meaning: a groom here is a person who looks after horses, at work in their building

explanation.surface: The location of a bridegroom, dressed in regimental kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' wants to be a bridegroom; here it is the horse attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-keeper works in the building where horses live; steady and constant things are even and consistent.

clue.text: Sort of garment for a single man

definitions.meaning: a swimsuit or overall made as one unit
a man in chess is a piece, so one man is one such unit

explanation.surface: A kind of clothing designed for a bachelor.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-unit item of clothing, such as a swimsuit; and a lone chessman, since a chess piece is called a man.

clue.text: Upper classes made up stories about descent

parts.note: A and B are the top social grades in the British classification of occupations

indicators.note: about signals the stories are turned round

parts.note: lies are fabricated tales

explanation.surface: The aristocracy invented tales concerning their pedigree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LIES into SEIL. 'descent' looks like lineage; it is going down a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope-controlled climb down a cliff or wall is a kind of descending.

clue.text: A seaman stole — I wasn't involved

parts.note: a boa is a feathery scarf or stole

indicators.note: involved means the letters are tangled together

explanation.surface: A sailor nicked something, but the speaker claims no part in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' wants to be a verb; it is the scarf. 'involved' rearranges IWASNT into TSWAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's officer in charge of rigging and deck crew is a sailor.

clue.text: Ballerinas missing a dance somewhere in Snowdonia

indicators.note: dance suggests the letters move about into a new order
missing means the following letter is dropped from the dancers

explanation.surface: Dancers without a partner perform in a Welsh mountain area.
explanation.walkthrough: BALLERINAS less an A, rearranged. Snowdonia is a mountainous national park in north Wales; Llanberis is a village there.
explanation.definitionFit: A village at the foot of Snowdon in north Wales, so a place in that region.

clue.text: Time gained with sleep in 24

indicators.note: in means the sleep goes inside the word for gained

parts.note: to have won is to have gained
a doze is a light sleep

explanation.surface: Extra time picked up by napping during a day's 24 hours.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' looks like a clue number referring elsewhere; it is just the figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The number twenty-four is two lots of twelve.

clue.text: Surprising action did warn a criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are corrupted into another order

explanation.surface: Someone tipped off a lawbreaker before a startling move.
explanation.walkthrough: A dawn raid is a surprise early-morning police swoop or, in finance, a sudden share-buying move.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden early-morning swoop is an action meant to take its target unawares.

clue.text: Some of the French opera supported by Poles

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the next piece sits below

parts.note: Norma is Bellini's opera
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Part of the French audience at an opera, held up by Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' wants to be people from Poland; here it is north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans were people of Normandy in northern France, a subset of the French.

clue.text: Bare bodies, shockingly, without a bit of raiment

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters go round the bit
shockingly suggests the letters are jolted into a new order
a bit of means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Naked forms, scandalously, wearing hardly any clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shockingly' rearranges BODIES into DISOBE, which goes round R, the first letter of 'raiment'.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip off one's clothes is to make oneself naked, a verb sense.

clue.text: Old coat cheers poet

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British thanks
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: An antique jacket raises a toast to a versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sleeveless tunic worn by medieval knights and heralds, an old garment.

clue.text: Robin is prepared to install central heating pipes

indicators.note: to install means the heating is fitted inside
is prepared indicates the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man named Robin is ready to fit radiators and pipework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is prepared' gives BRONI; 'pipes' wants to be plumbing, matching the heating, but means airways.
explanation.definitionFit: The two main airways branching from the windpipe into the lungs are tubes in the body.

clue.text: A writer's attributes

parts.note: a scribe is a writer, and the possessive gives an extra S

explanation.surface: The characteristics belonging to an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attributes' looks like a noun; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit something to a cause or person is to attribute it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stand by Jack in some evacuated capital

indicators.note: in means the stand and jack go inside
evacuated means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the Kop is a terraced stand at a football ground, famously Liverpool's
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: Wait beside a man named Jack in an emptied city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand by' wants to mean wait; 'Stand' is the Kop, 'by' just joins. The capital is that of North Macedonia.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief city of North Macedonia is that nation's capital.

clue.text: Start to swing and get high, say

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: to peak is to reach the highest point

explanation.surface: Get going on the swing and soar, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak is to utter words, which is what saying something means.

clue.text: Jokes not fine and dandy with American college

indicators.note: not means the letters for the phrase that follows are left out

parts.note: OK means all right, fine and dandy

explanation.surface: Gags that are not all right go down with an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: JOKES without OK leaves JES. Jesus College exists at both Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus is the name of a college at Oxford and at Cambridge.

clue.text: South Africa blocking Arab free market

indicators.note: blocking means the country code sits inside the other letters
free suggests the letters are loosed into a new order

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: South Africa obstructs an Arab trader's open market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' turns ARAB into BAAR; 'free market' wants to be the definition, but only 'market' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern market street of shops and stalls, or a sale of goods.

clue.text: Dull players finished first

indicators.note: first says the word for finished comes before the players

parts.note: something over is finished
a cast is the players in a production

explanation.surface: Boring actors were done before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey sky full of cloud is gloomy and lacking brightness.

clue.text: Responsibility a felon usually conceals

indicators.note: conceals means the letters lie inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A criminal's duty is typically hidden away.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or duty laid on someone, Latin for load.

clue.text: Food from a tree filling people with intelligence

indicators.note: filling means the tree goes inside

parts.note: spies gather intelligence, secret information
teak is a tropical hardwood tree

explanation.surface: Something to eat from a tree that stuffs clever folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence' wants to mean cleverness; it is secret information.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry cases of meat are an example of food.
